prompts.text:
A home Wi-Fi network works by using a router and an access point to connect devices. The router acts as the central hub, directing all the devices to connect to it. The access point, which is usually a wireless router, is connected to the router and is responsible for directing all the devices to connect to it.

When a device wants to connect to the internet, it sends a request to the router. The router then forwards the request to the access point. The access point then forwards the request to the wireless router, which in turn forwards it to the internet. This process is called "wireless bridging."

The wireless router then uses the access point's radio channels to send the video stream from the internet to the laptop. The laptop, which is connected to the wireless router, receives the video stream and displays it on its screen.

When two devices transmit at once, they can use the same wireless router and access point. This allows them to share the same Wi-Fi network and access the internet simultaneously.
